title: Second-variable naturality of Ext-cohomology for a locally free first argument
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $\mathcal G,\mathcal G'$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules with a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$. Under the canonical isomorphisms $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\cong H^i(X,\mathcal F^\vee\otimes\mathcal G)$ and $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G')\cong H^i(X,\mathcal F^\vee\otimes\mathcal G')$ of [lem-sc-ext-locally-free], the map on Ext induced by $\varphi$ is the cohomology map induced by $1_{\mathcal F^\vee}\otimes\varphi$. Thus the canonical Ext-cohomology identification is natural in the second module variable.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06XR (derived-lemma-compute-ext-resolutions), together with Cohomology Tag 01DZ (derived functor maps are natural)

proof.text: Write $T=\mathcal F^\vee\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}-$ on $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, which has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution], $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,-)$ is the right derived functor of $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,-)$ computed by injective resolutions: for an injective resolution $\varepsilon:\mathcal G\to I^\bullet$ the class of a cocycle $f:\mathcal F\to I^i$ goes to $\varepsilon[i]^{-1}\circ f$. The canonical isomorphism of [lem-sc-ext-locally-free] is the composite of this identification with $\mathcal H^i(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,I^\bullet))\cong\mathcal H^i(\Gamma(X,T(I^\bullet)))$ (global sections of the evaluation isomorphism [lem-sc-ext-evaluation], via the global-sections clause of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]) and the derived-composite comparison $c^i:\mathcal H^i(\Gamma(X,T(I^\bullet)))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^i\Gamma(T(\mathcal G))=H^i(X,\mathcal F^\vee\otimes\mathcal G)$ of [lem-sc-ext-derived-composite], which is the comparison map of item 2 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] for the resolution $T(\varepsilon):T(\mathcal G)\to T(I^\bullet)$.

Hypotheses for the comparison. $\mathcal F^\vee$ is finite locally free (on each $V_a$ with $\mathcal F|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$, [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives $\mathcal F^\vee|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$), so $T$ is exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. For an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module $I$, $T(I)\cong\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal F,I)$ by [lem-sc-ext-evaluation]; $\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal F,-)$ is right adjoint to $\mathcal F\otimes-$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm], and $\mathcal F\otimes-$ is exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact], so $T(I)$ is injective by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], hence $\Gamma(X,-)$-acyclic by item 1 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]. Thus for injective resolutions $\varepsilon:\mathcal G\to I^\bullet$, $\varepsilon':\mathcal G'\to I'^\bullet$, the maps $T(\varepsilon)$, $T(\varepsilon')$ are resolutions by $\Gamma$-acyclic objects.

Lift $\varphi$: since the augmented complex of $I^\bullet$ is exact and the $I'^m$ are injective, there is a morphism of complexes $\psi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ with $\psi^0\circ\varepsilon=\varepsilon'\circ\varphi$ (degreewise extension using injectivity). Then $\psi\circ\varepsilon=\varepsilon'\circ\varphi$ as maps $\mathcal G[0]\to I'^\bullet$, so for a cocycle $f:\mathcal F\to I^i$ one has $\varphi[i]\circ\varepsilon[i]^{-1}\circ f=\varepsilon'[i]^{-1}\circ\psi[i]\circ f$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. By the explicit formula of Step 1, the map $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\varphi)$ (postcomposition with $\varphi[i]$) corresponds to $\mathcal H^i(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\psi))$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06XR (derived-lemma-compute-ext-resolutions): morphisms into an injective complex

proof.text: By the naturality in the coefficient module of the evaluation isomorphism [lem-sc-ext-evaluation], applied degreewise to $\psi^m:I^m\to I'^m$ and followed by global sections ([def-pur-sheaf-hom]), the identification $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,I^\bullet)\cong\Gamma(X,T(I^\bullet))$ of Step 1 carries $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\psi)$ to $\Gamma(X,T(\psi))$; hence $\mathcal H^i(\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\psi))$ corresponds to $\mathcal H^i(\Gamma(X,T(\psi)))$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: evaluation isomorphism, natural in the coefficient module

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural] with $v=\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, $F=T(\mathcal G)$, $F'=T(\mathcal G')$, the $\Gamma$-acyclic resolutions $r=T(\varepsilon)$, $r'=T(\varepsilon')$ of Step 2, $h=1_{\mathcal F^\vee}\otimes\varphi=T(\varphi)$ and the morphism of complexes $T(\psi)$; its hypothesis $T(\psi^0)\circ T(\varepsilon)=T(\varepsilon')\circ T(\varphi)$ is $T$ applied to the equation of Step 3. Its comparison maps are the maps $c^i$, $c'^i$ of Step 1, and it gives $c'^i\circ\mathcal H^i(\Gamma(X,T(\psi)))=R^i\Gamma(1\otimes\varphi)\circ c^i$, where $R^i\Gamma(1\otimes\varphi)=H^i(1_{\mathcal F^\vee}\otimes\varphi)$ by [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. Combined with Steps 1, 3 and 4, the Ext map induced by $\varphi$ corresponds to the cohomology map induced by $1_{\mathcal F^\vee}\otimes\varphi$.
